newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PRICE WINS HERITAGE GOLF TOURNAMENT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PRICE WINS HERITAGE GOLF TOURNAMENT.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Nick Price led throughout the final round on his
way to a six-stroke victory at the $1.5 million Heritage
Classic golf tournament on Sunday.
Price, who began the day with a two-stroke cushion over
Brad Faxon, doubled his lead after seven holes and was never
in danger after that on his way to a five-under-par 66 in
pleasant conditions at the tight Harbour Town course.
He birdied the final hole to finish at 15-under 269, while
Swede Jesper Parnevik (66) and American Faxon (70) tied for
second on 275.
British Open champion Tom Lehman (72) finished tied at
fourth at six-under 278, which was enough to earn him the
world number one ranking for the first time.
Price He displaced Australian Greg Norman, who had been at
the top for a record 96 consecutive weeks.
Price, winner of three major championships, was ranked
number one in the world for 43 weeks until June, 1995, when he
was ousted by Norman.
But the day belonged to Price, who received $270,000 for
his 15th PGA Tour victory to jump to sixth on this year's
money list.
Price, 39, won twice in jointly-sanctioned European and
South African Tour events in South Africa in February, but
this was his first PGA Tour victory since the Canadian Open in
September, 1994.
"We all know that this is the hardest tour in the world to
win on (although) the two wins in South Africa were a help in
getting me to win today," said Price.
He dedicated his victory to his caddie, Jeff "Squeeky"
Medlen, who is in hospital in Columbus, Ohio, battling chronic
leukaemia.
"I can't tell you how happy I am. There has been a lot
going on off the course for me. To put it aside and play has
been pretty tough," Price said.
"I won this for Squeek. It's important for me to win, but
it's more important for him to know how many people are
pulling for him. I think he knows that now," he said.
"I was so focused out there today. I didn't make a bogey
anywhere. I didn't give (Faxon) any openings, and I think that
was a little discouraging for him.
"I think my long game has been hardened by the fact I
haven't putted well the last year-and-a-half. Towards the end
of last year I honestly didn't think I was ever going to putt
well again," Price said.
"Then I switched putters two weeks ago and I got on the
putting green at Augusta (at last week's Masters) and I had a
beautiful feel with this putter. Now my putting is coming
together."
Parnevik, meanwhile, enhanced his European Ryder Cup
claims with his fourth second-placing of the year on the PGA
Tour.
"I was really happy to bring it back," said Parnevik, who
was four over par after 11 holes of the first round.
Parnevik said he would continue to play most of his golf
on the PGA Tour this year, rather than rejoin the European
Tour in an effort to win points toward making this year's
Ryder Cup team.
"I don't think I am going to rejoin the European Tour as a
full-time member. It's too tough a schedule right now. I want
to give myself a full chance to play over here this year."
